title: carmt: ARMT + Gated DeltaNet-2 in one CUDA file - speed vs the PyTorch / fla implementation
date: 2026-11-12 (updated after the GEMM tuning / backward changes)
figure_caption: GDN-2 370M + ARMT (32 memory tokens, 8 x 1024-token segments), bf16, RTX 6000 Ada. Same parameters, same outputs.

setup.precision: bf16 autocast (fp32 master weights), as in train.py
setup.original: recurrent_armt.RecurrentARMTForCausalLM with fla 0.6 Triton kernels, gradient checkpointing per (layer, segment) as train.py runs it; without checkpointing it does not fit in 48 GB
setup.carmt: carmt/armt.cu (CUDA + cuBLAS), default bf16 build, carmt.accelerate(model)

long_context_note: one forward call per length, output_logits='last', no labels, no grad, batch 1. Both implementations run segment by segment in constant memory (the original since its fix: one segment embedded at a time, only the last segment's hidden states kept). carmt's ~0.2 GB extra is mostly its packed bf16 weight copy. Device memory = cudaMemGetInfo difference over the call (model weights excluded).

train_1gpu_peak_gb.source: bench_rtx6000_bf16.json, torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated (carmt allocates through PyTorch's caching allocator)

train_ddp_logged_gb.source: train.py's logged 'mem' (max_memory_allocated) in the DDP runs; carmt adds the flat fp32 gradient buffer and its training stores

training_parity.run: 100 optimizer steps, 2-GPU DDP, identical data stream and seed (carmt/records/train_ddp_rtx6000_*.jsonl, previous build); the current build's 30-step runs log the same losses to 4 decimals and identical eval losses
training_parity.train_loss: within 2e-4 at every logged step (steps 10-100): equal to 4 decimals at 9 of the 10, step 90 2.3994 vs 2.3992
training_parity.eval: val 2.4039 / 2.4007 / 2.4012 at steps 0 / 50 / 100 for both; val_long within 1e-4

equivalence.fp32_logits_vs_exact_reference: <= 1e-4 relative across 9 configurations (the original's own TF32 kernels: ~1e-3)
equivalence.bf16_gradients_real_dims: per-parameter relative-norm error vs fp32: median 0.84x the original's own bf16 error
equivalence.distributed: DDP, DDP + grad accumulation (+ no_sync), DeepSpeed ZeRO-1 / ZeRO-2: gradients match the reference; bf16 370M DDP and ZeRO-2 vs single-process carmt <= 4e-7 (carmt/records/dist_check_2x_rtx5880.log)

profile_train_step.note: 176 TFLOP = forward + recomputed forward (w3 on the memory rows only) + backward of the model's linear layers; the 1.64 s of cuBLAS time also includes the scan's chunk-batched GEMMs, so 107 TFLOPS is a lower bound for the model GEMMs. RTX 6000 Ada dense bf16 peak: 364 TFLOPS.

long_context_loss_mode.note: with labels (loss over every token) the original's forward still keeps all hidden states: one call needs 20.7 GB at 1M tokens and runs out of memory at 4.2M; streamed in 64k pieces with state= it takes 3.4 GB at 20.3k tok/s. carmt computes the loss per segment: 1.44 GB and 84.7k tok/s at 10.5M tokens in one call.

changes_since_first_report: GEMM algorithm tuning: on first use of each shape, cuBLASLt's candidates are timed against cuBLAS's default and the fastest kept; choices are persisted per GPU model and cuBLAS version (carmt/.gemm_cache_*), so DDP ranks and later runs use the same kernels (carmt/records/gemm_tune_rtx6000.log)
the backward's recompute runs the MLP output projection on the memory-token rows only

the backward is one autograd node per layer, so DDP / ZeRO can reduce a layer's gradients while the layers below run: no measurable gain in the 2-GPU job (36.1k tok/s with and without; exposed all-reduce 0.24 vs 0.32 s per optimizer step: carmt/records/ddp_layer_nodes_rtx6000.log)

measured and dropped: a two-stream schedule (two full training steps on two streams are 2-8% slower than back to back: carmt/records/overlap_ceiling_rtx6000.log); a lower-register rewrite of the conv/gate kernel (no change)

bug fix: a script keeping an accelerated model alive until interpreter exit segfaulted on exit (code 139); C contexts are now freed in an atexit handler (test_process_exits_cleanly_with_a_model_alive_at_exit)

review fix: the GEMM tuning no longer holds the cache file's lock while timing (the timing synchronizes the training stream, which with per-layer backward nodes may wait on another rank's collective); concurrent tunings of one shape resolve to the first entry written. dist_check passes from an empty cache
